summary: TASK-139 is approval-ready as a plan for stop-the-world, time-warped Alpamayo CARLA control. It correctly separates time-warped closed-loop control from real-time VLA control, preserves fake/blocked/real backend labels, and defines concrete proof plus a metric path without overwriting the active root autoresearch session.

finding_log.summary: Real Alpamayo mode depends on TASK-134 or an equivalent local inference seam, so implementation should start with fake and blocked backends.
evidence: The ticket names TASK-134 as a dependency and explicitly keeps fake/blocked proof unblocked.
Execution steps 3-5 sequence fake backend, blocked backend, then real Alpamayo integration.
finding_log.next_action: Implement the fake backend first and do not claim real model evidence until TASK-134 or a real Alpamayo backend is available.

finding_log.summary: The ticket-scoped autoresearch session is intentionally deferred until the scorer exists, which is correct but should be revisited immediately after `score-vla-drive` lands.
evidence: The root autoresearch session already targets `submission_readiness_score`.
The planned metric command cannot be dry-run before `score-vla-drive` is implemented.
finding_log.next_action: After `score-vla-drive --metric-only` exists, initialize `tickets/TASK-139/autoresearch/` and dry-run the metric once before optimization.

rubric_sections.name: spec-contract
findings: The ticket targets one coherent outcome: repeated current-state VLA decisions driving short CARLA segments in time-warped simulation.
Acceptance criteria distinguish fake, blocked, and real evidence and prevent real-time overclaims.
rubric_sections.next_action: Approve for build after TASK-134 dependency expectations are understood.

rubric_sections.name: implementation-plan
findings: The plan names callable seams, typed payloads, and an ordered fake -> blocked -> real backend sequence.
The main bloat risk is CARLA helper extraction; the plan contains it by requiring a focused module and avoiding broad runner refactors.
rubric_sections.next_action: Build the focused simulator loop module first, then wire CLI and scorer.

rubric_sections.name: integration-readiness
findings: Dependencies on TASK-134 and GPU runtime are explicit and safely contained by fake/blocked modes.
Claim boundaries align with MEM-0034 and MEM-0038 while upgrading from open-loop reasoning to time-warped model-driven control.
rubric_sections.next_action: Keep real Alpamayo integration behind a backend seam and preserve blocked artifacts when runtime dependencies are absent.

rubric_sections.name: evidence-quality
findings: The planned evidence packet maps every major claim to a concrete artifact: checkpoint, prediction, trajectory, control trace, applied segment, frames, tracks, score, and video.
Autoresearch is handled responsibly by preserving the existing root session and deferring ticket-scoped initialization until the metric command can be dry-run.
rubric_sections.next_action: Once implemented, collect fake-backend proof first, then optional Kasm real Alpamayo proof.

next_action: Move TASK-139 to building when ready, starting with fake backend and scorer implementation before attempting real Alpamayo/CARLA runtime proof.
